blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Cross-docking and modern distribution strategies let a company move goods faster while holding less inventory. In practice, this means deciding which products flow straight through — cross-dock — and which actually need to stop, rest, and be stored the classic way. Getting this split right is worth more than any single process improvement.

Products with steady demand, predictable inbound, and short shelf lives are natural cross-dock candidates. Irregular, long-life products are usually better stored and distributed the traditional way. A company that treats both with the same rulebook ends up slow at one and wasteful at the other.

The real advantage comes from mixing. Cross-dock what can be cross-docked, store what must be stored, and design the warehouse so that both flows coexist without tripping over each other.

items.q: According to the text, what is worth more than any single process improvement?
options: Getting the cross-dock / store split right
items.why: "Getting this split right is worth more than any single process improvement."

items.q: Which products are described as natural cross-dock candidates?
options: Irregular products with a long shelf life
Products with steady demand and short shelf lives
High-value products that need extra security
items.why: "steady demand, predictable inbound, and short shelf lives are natural cross-dock candidates."

items.q: The author suggests that using the same rulebook for both flows will…
options: make the company slow at one and wasteful at the other
items.why: Inferência: "ends up slow at one and wasteful at the other" — o manual único prejudica os dois fluxos.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Every product should be pushed through cross-docking to save time.
Some products are better off being stored than cross-docked.
The best warehouses let both flows coexist.
The right split matters more than any single improvement.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende a mistura — forçar tudo pelo cross-dock contraria o argumento central.

items.q: What does "without tripping over each other" suggest about the two flows?
options: They should be designed so neither one blocks the other
One flow should always have priority
They should be handled by the same team
They must never share the same building
items.why: Inferência: os dois fluxos coexistem no mesmo armazém sem se atrapalharem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando o redesenho do centro de distribuição. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Alright, let me walk you through the new layout for the regional centre. The target is simple: sixty per cent of the volume is cross-docked straight through, and the remaining forty per cent is stored the classic way. The hard part is making sure neither flow blocks the other.

So here is how it works. Inbound trucks are unloaded at the north doors. Fast-moving items with steady demand are scanned, sorted, and reloaded within a couple of hours — they never touch a shelf. Everything else is moved to the storage zone on the south side, where it waits until an order pulls it.

Two things get handled separately. Temperature-sensitive goods are routed through their own cold dock, and irregular, slow-moving stock is stored deeper in the racks so it doesn't clog the fast lanes.

One point I want to stress: this split is not fixed. The distribution strategy is reviewed every month, because demand shifts. A product that cross-docks well in spring might need to be stored by autumn. If we design the floor to be flexible now, we won't have to rebuild it every time the numbers move.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the target split Oliver describes for the regional centre?
items.why: "sixty per cent of the volume is cross-docked… the remaining forty per cent is stored."

items.q: According to Oliver, what happens to fast-moving items with steady demand?
options: They are routed through the cold dock
They wait until an order pulls them
They are scanned, sorted, and reloaded within a couple of hours
They are stored deep in the racks
items.why: "scanned, sorted, and reloaded within a couple of hours — they never touch a shelf."

items.q: Which goods are handled separately from the two main flows?
options: Any item over a certain weight
items.why: "Temperature-sensitive goods are routed through their own cold dock."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the split is reviewed every month?
options: Because demand shifts and a product's best flow can change
Because trucks arrive on a monthly schedule
items.why: Inferência: "demand shifts… a product that cross-docks well in spring might need to be stored by autumn."

items.q: What is Oliver's main reason for designing a flexible floor now?
options: To reduce the number of employees needed
To store every product on the south side
To avoid rebuilding the layout every time demand changes
To make the cold dock larger
items.why: Inferência: "If we design the floor to be flexible now, we won't have to rebuild it every time the numbers move."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "These pallets will cross-dock and never enter storage." To cross-dock means to…
options: move goods straight from inbound to outbound with little or no storage
keep goods in the warehouse for weeks
items.why: Cross-dock = passar a mercadoria direto da recepção para o embarque, quase sem estoque.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Items with steady demand are predictable, so we can schedule them tightly." Steady demand means…
options: demand that jumps up and down
demand that is consistent and predictable
items.why: Steady demand = demanda estável, previsível ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Fresh produce has a ___, so it must move quickly."
items.why: Short shelf life = vida útil curta; produtos frescos precisam girar rápido.

items.q: "Demand for this line is irregular, so we store it instead of cross-docking." Irregular means…
items.why: Irregular = irregular, sem padrão previsível — por isso é melhor estocar.

items.q: "We designed the floor so both flows can coexist." To coexist means to…
items.why: To coexist = coexistir, funcionar lado a lado sem se atrapalhar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Operations still has to sign off on the new layout." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the cross-dock model site by site." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The night shift pushed back on the new dock schedule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo proposto.

items.q: "Steady inbound helps us keep up with the fast lanes." To keep up with means to…
options: move at the same pace and not fall behind
items.why: Keep up with = acompanhar o ritmo, não ficar para trás.

items.q: "Trimming that shelf time really moved the needle on delivery speed." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, gerar um efeito perceptível.
